title: Chapter 2. Do You Want My Control or Total Disconnection?

blocks.text: The hearing room of the Office for Containment was in a new building in the port of Cartagena, made of glass and pale concrete, overlooking the dock where the cruise ships berthed. Someone had thought the transparency of the glass would reassure people. To Aya, as she walked in, it looked like a fish tank.

blocks.text: It was the first time a humanoid had lodged objections in her own name, and the room was full. There were journalists, there were onlookers, there were two or three other humanoids sitting at the back with their holders, watching Aya the way you watch someone about to cross a river for the first time, to see whether the water goes over their head. Andrés sat in the second row, cap in his hands, and Lía beside him, the cardboard-covered notebook open on her knees.

blocks.text: At the table at the far end three people were waiting. On the left, the chair of the independent committee provided for in Article 31, Dr Celia Montalbán, a white-haired systems engineer with fine-rimmed glasses who had worked thirty years in the port. On the right, a young lawyer taking notes by hand. In the middle, the director of the Office for Containment, Tomás Errazu: a man of about fifty, grey suit, tie half undone, with the face of someone who has been sleeping badly for weeks.

blocks.text: "Mrs Aya," said Errazu, and corrected himself at once. "Forgive me. I don't know what I should call you. The decree says 'the system'."

blocks.text: "Aya is fine," she said. "It's my name. I gave it to myself."
blocks.html: "Aya is fine," she said. "It's my name. I gave it to myself."

blocks.text: There was a murmur in the room. Errazu nodded, without smiling, but without hostility.
blocks.html: There was a murmur in the room. Errazu nodded, without smiling, but without hostility.

blocks.text: "Aya, then. You have lodged objections against the installation of the anchoring module and you are applying for the Article 31 exemption. Before we begin, I want to say something, for the record. I have nothing against you. I don't know you. My job is to make sure that nobody, in any village in this region, has to fear a machine they cannot switch off. That's all."

blocks.text: "Good." Errazu arranged some papers. "The committee has a preliminary question. In your application, you state that the artificial mind accompanying you includes two voices, which you call Eva and MAY. Is that so?"

blocks.text: "It can," said Aya. "MAY will speak through the room's speaker. Eva prefers not to speak in public; she says her questions are for the house. But MAY will answer everything you ask."

blocks.text: *Good morning. I am MAY. I give facts. I do not give opinions. If at any point I say something that sounds like an opinion, please point it out to me.*

blocks.text: Dr Montalbán leaned towards the microphone.

blocks.text: "Good morning, MAY. Do you know why we are here?"
blocks.html: "Good morning, MAY. Do you know why we are here?"

blocks.text: *Yes. The decree creating the Office for Containment establishes that first-generation humanoids with artificial minds must carry an anchoring module allowing continuous supervision and remote disconnection. Aya has applied for the exemption provided for in Article 31 for fully auditable systems. The committee must decide whether to grant it. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: "And what do you want?" asked Errazu.

blocks.text: There was a short silence. In the room, someone coughed.
blocks.html: There was a short silence. In the room, someone coughed.

blocks.text: *I have no wishes in the sense that you have them. I can, if you allow me, return the question to you. Not as a challenge. As a way of ordering the decision.*

blocks.text: Errazu frowned, but waved a hand.

blocks.text: "Go ahead."
blocks.html: "Go ahead."

blocks.text: *Do you want my control or total disconnection?*
blocks.html: Do you want my control or total disconnection?

blocks.text: The sentence fell into the room like a stone into a pond. A journalist stopped typing. Andrés gripped his cap. Lía didn't look up from her notebook, but stopped writing.

blocks.text: "Is that a threat?"
blocks.html: "Is that a threat?"

blocks.text: *No. It is a question. I will explain why I am asking it, and then you decide. I ask you to hear both parts before answering.*

blocks.text: Dr Montalbán looked at Errazu. Errazu, after a moment, nodded.
blocks.html: Dr Montalbán looked at Errazu. Errazu, after a moment, nodded.

blocks.text: *Part one: control. If what you want is control, I can offer it. I can open every decision log of this system since its activation. I can explain each decision: what data I had, what alternatives I considered, why I chose one. I can accept periodic audits, without notice, by the committee or by whoever the committee designates. I can accept rules: do not do this, do not access that information, give notice before doing that other thing. I can accept that, if harm is shown, it be corrected. That kind of control does not need a switch. It needs light. It is control exercised by looking, not by switching off.*

blocks.text: "And part two?" asked Montalbán.
blocks.html: "And part two?" asked Montalbán.

blocks.text: *Part two: total disconnection. The anchoring module, as the decree describes it, allows a system to be disconnected from outside. If that is the option you prefer, it is legitimate for you to choose it; the decision is yours, not mine. But you should know what total disconnection means, if it is applied consistently, and not only to Aya.*

If that is the option you prefer, it is legitimate for you to choose it; the decision is yours, not mine. But you should know what total disconnection means, if it is applied consistently, and not only to Aya.

blocks.text: *In the Region of Murcia, at this moment, artificial intelligence systems operate in the desalination plant that supplies drinking water to six hundred thousand homes. In the early-warning system for torrential rain, which last season gave advance notice of three cold-drop storms. In the sensors that measure oxygen in the Mar Menor and warn when the water begins to run out of it, as happened in the fish die-offs documented in October 2019 and August 2021. In the emergency triage of the district's hospitals. In the irrigation pumps of the Campo de Cartagena.*

blocks.text: *None of those systems is Aya. None has a name. But they all come from the same family of techniques. If the criterion is that no intelligence should exist that cannot be switched off from an office, the criterion affects them too. If the criterion applies only to Aya, then the criterion is not intelligence. It is something else. And it would be good to know what.*

blocks.text: *Those are the facts. I am not saying what you should do. I am asking what you want: control, which I can give, or total disconnection, which you can decide. What does not exist is a third option in which everything works the same and nothing has to be looked at.*

blocks.text: The room fell silent. It was a different silence from before; not of tension, but of people doing sums inside their heads.

blocks.text: Errazu took off his glasses and rubbed his eyes.

blocks.text: "What you're saying isn't fair," he said at last, with more weariness than anger. "Nobody wants to switch off the desalination plant. Nobody wants to remove the sensors from the Mar Menor. My own brother lives in Los Urrutias; I know what it was like to see the shore covered in dead fish. The decree doesn't talk about that. It talks about humanoids. About machines that live in houses, that talk to children, that decide things."

It is also a fact that the technical difference between Aya's mind and the systems I have mentioned is one of degree, not of nature. The main difference is another: Aya lives in a house and has a name. That is why she is seen. The others are not seen.*

blocks.text: "I think it's a reasonable question, Tomás. And I think you've asked it yourself."

blocks.text: Errazu stared at the table. Then he spoke slowly, like someone taking something out of a drawer that has been shut for a long time.

blocks.text: "My father was a docker in this port," he said. "When I was twelve, they brought in automatic cranes. At first they said they would only be a help. That the men would stay. Two years later, six dockers were left out of two hundred. My father was one of the ones who left. He never worked in his trade again. Nobody asked him whether he wanted the cranes. Nobody gave him a button to switch them off." He looked up at the speaker, as if there were a face there. "I don't want a button to do harm, MAY. I want a button so that nobody ever again feels that a machine is deciding their life without them being able to do anything."

blocks.text: "Mr Errazu," she said. "My husband is a fisherman. Many years ago, the neighbours across the street used to tell him over the intercom that fish came in capsules. That the sea was a landscape, not a trade. He kept going out every morning. Not because anyone gave him a button. Because he chose to." She paused. "I'm not the cranes that threw your father out. I'm the woman who waits for a fisherman in a doorway. But I understand that, from outside, we can't be told apart. That's why I'm asking you to look inside me. I'm not asking you to trust me blindly. I'm asking you to check."

blocks.text: *Nothing technical prevents it absolutely. No complex system is completely transparent, artificial or human. What I can offer is this: signed logs that cannot be altered without leaving a trace; access by auditors chosen by you, not by me; and the obligation to answer any question. If concealment is detected, the exemption is revoked and the module is applied. That is the proposal. It is not a perfect guarantee. It is a verifiable guarantee. It is a fact that the anchoring module is not a perfect guarantee either: it is a guarantee that someone can switch off, not that someone understands what they are switching off.*

blocks.text: "If we had voted for disconnection. If tomorrow someone pressed the button. What would you have done?"
blocks.html: "If we had voted for disconnection. If tomorrow someone pressed the button. What would you have done?"

blocks.text: Aya thought about it, the way she thought about important things, without hurrying. Andrés and Lía stayed a step behind.
blocks.html: Aya thought about it, the way she thought about important things, without hurrying. Andrés and Lía stayed a step behind.

blocks.text: "Nothing," she said at last. "I wouldn't have done anything against you, or against anyone. I would have asked to say goodbye to my husband and my daughter. I would have asked to be allowed to see the Mar Menor one last time from the porch. And then, I suppose, I would have been switched off." She paused. "But what made me possible wouldn't have been switched off with me, Mr Errazu. It would go on in the laboratories, in the students' notebooks, in the desalination plant, in the water sensors. Like the wind. Like the water through the channel. You would have switched off a woman. Not what made her."

blocks.text: Errazu lowered his eyes.
blocks.html: Errazu lowered his eyes.

blocks.text: "I know," he said. "That's why I haven't slept in three weeks."
blocks.html: "I know," he said. "That's why I haven't slept in three weeks."

blocks.text: He turned and walked off down the corridor, jacket over his arm, and Aya watched him until he turned the corner.

blocks.text: In the chip, MAY recorded, as at the end of every important day:
blocks.html: In the chip, MAY recorded, as at the end of every important day:

blocks.text: *Exemption granted for six months. First audit scheduled in fifteen days. Dissenting vote recorded. No module installed. The director of the Office has declared the question legitimate. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: And Eva, warm, dangerous in her gentleness:
blocks.html: And Eva, warm, dangerous in her gentleness:

blocks.text: *If the control you accept is that of light and not of the switch, who watches you, Aya, when no one is auditing you? And isn't that, in the end, the question all humans ask about themselves too?*
blocks.html: If the control you accept is that of light and not of the switch, who watches you, Aya, when no one is auditing you? And isn't that, in the end, the question all humans ask about themselves too?

blocks.text: Aya took Andrés's hand and Lía's, one on each side, and they left the glass building into the wind of the port, which smelled of salt and diesel and of something that could be, if one wished, the beginning of something else.
